paraphrase: Obtain consent through a clear affirmative action by the data principal, never by silence, pre-ticked boxes or continued use.
Make consent free and unconditional, with no term that waives a legal right or permits processing the law forbids.
State the specified purpose in every consent request so the consent is informed.
Write each consent request in clear, plain language.
Offer the consent request in English or in a language from the Eighth Schedule at the data principal's choice.
List each purpose as a separate item in the consent request when data is used for more than one purpose.
Record the data principal's consent against each specific purpose rather than as one blanket consent.
Let data principals withdraw consent as easily as they gave it.
Stop processing, and have processors stop, once consent is withdrawn unless a law requires retention.
Use only Consent Managers that are registered with the Data Protection Board.
Confirm the Consent Manager gives data principals an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform to manage consent.
Obtain verifiable consent from a parent before processing the personal data of a child under 18.
Obtain verifiable consent from a lawful guardian before processing the personal data of a person with a disability.
Verify that the person consenting is an identifiable adult parent or a validly appointed guardian.
Present a notice before or together with every consent request, not only in a site footer.
Itemize in the notice the personal data to be collected.
State in the notice the specified purposes and the goods, services or uses each purpose enables.
Tell the data principal in the notice how to withdraw consent and exercise their rights.
Tell the data principal in the notice how to complain to the Data Protection Board.
Write the notice so it is understandable on its own, without reading other documents.
Offer the notice in English or in a language from the Eighth Schedule at the data principal's choice.
Give data principals a notice, as soon as reasonably practicable, for personal data collected before the Act applied.
Describe in that notice the personal data held and the purposes it is processed for.
Include in the notice the contact details of the officer who answers data principals' questions.
Publish those contact details prominently on the website or app.
Process personal data only for the purpose the data principal consented to.
Where no consent is held, process personal data only for a purpose the Act treats as a legitimate use.
Identify every case where personal data is processed without consent under the legitimate-use provisions.
Document the legitimate-use basis relied on for each such case.
Collect only the personal data that is necessary for the stated purpose.
Erase personal data once the purpose it was collected for is no longer served.
Retain personal data beyond that purpose only where a law requires it, and name the law.
Maintain a documented retention schedule that sets a period or erasure trigger for each data category or purpose.
Run systematic or automated procedures that erase personal data when the purpose ends or consent is withdrawn.
Retain personal data, traffic data and processing logs for at least the minimum period the Rules require before erasure.
Check that retention and deletion settings on systems holding personal data match the schedule.
Ensure personal data is complete, accurate and consistent before it is used to make a decision affecting the data principal.
Ensure personal data is complete, accurate and consistent before it is disclosed to another data fiduciary.
Implement reasonable technical safeguards to protect personal data and prevent breaches.
Implement reasonable organizational safeguards to protect personal data and prevent breaches.
Encrypt personal data at rest.
Encrypt personal data in transit.
Restrict access to personal data to authorized personnel on a least-privilege basis.
Hold a valid written contract with every data processor that handles personal data for the organization.
Require each processor by contract to implement appropriate security safeguards.
Require each processor by contract to process personal data only on the organization's instructions.
Publish how a data principal can request information about their personal data and what identifier to give.
Provide on request a summary of the personal data being processed.
Provide on request a summary of the processing activities carried out on that data.
Identify on request the other data fiduciaries and processors the data was shared with and what was shared.
Correct personal data on request when it is inaccurate or misleading.
Complete personal data on request when it is incomplete.
Let data principals request erasure of the personal data they gave consent for, at any time.
Erase the data on request unless retention is necessary for the specified purpose or to comply with law.
Provide an accessible way for data principals to register grievances.
Designate a person or officer who handles those grievances.
Respond to each grievance within a reasonable, defined time.
Tell the data principal about their right to approach the Data Protection Board when a grievance is unresolved.
Let data principals nominate another individual to exercise their rights.
Honor the nominee's exercise of those rights on the data principal's death or incapacity.
Do not track children.
Do not carry out behavioral monitoring of children.
Do not direct targeted advertising at children.
Do not process children's personal data in a way that harms their well-being.
Verify the age of users in order to identify children.
Apply the child protections, including parental consent, to every user identified as a child.
Appoint a Data Protection Officer when designated a Significant Data Fiduciary.
Ensure the Data Protection Officer is an individual based in India.
Make the Data Protection Officer responsible to the board or equivalent governing body, with the reporting line documented.
Name the Data Protection Officer as the contact point for the grievance mechanism.
Appoint an independent data auditor to evaluate compliance with the Act.
Conduct a data protection impact assessment of processing activities and the risks to data principals.
Repeat the impact assessment at the prescribed periodic interval.
Audit compliance with the Act and Rules at the prescribed periodic interval.
Have the auditor report significant observations to the Data Protection Board.
Maintain auditable records of when, how and for what purpose each data principal gave consent.
Obtain fresh consent before processing personal data for a new or changed purpose.
Give data principals working controls to give or withhold consent for each purpose, so partial consent is possible.
Keep access to the service independent of consent to processing that the service does not need.
Avoid dark patterns when collecting consent.
Transfer personal data outside India only to countries or territories not restricted by the Central Government.
Maintain an inventory of cross-border data flows.
Track Central Government notifications that restrict transfers to specific countries or territories.
Do not transfer personal data to a country or territory restricted by such a notification.
Comply with any stricter sectoral law in force in India on transfers outside India.
Store the categories of personal data in India that the Central Government requires to be localized.
Notify the Data Protection Board promptly of any personal data breach.
Follow the prescribed form, content and timeline when reporting the breach to the Board.
Notify each affected data principal of a personal data breach.
Follow the prescribed form and content when notifying data principals.
Cover detection of personal data breaches in a documented incident response plan.
Cover containment of personal data breaches in the documented plan.
Cover investigation of personal data breaches in the documented plan.
Cover notification of regulators and data principals in the documented plan.
Cover remediation of personal data breaches in the documented plan.
Maintain a register of all personal data breaches.
Record in the register the facts and effects of each breach.
Record in the register the remedial actions taken for each breach.
